experiment: 2x2 on our chain: kernel spectral filter on/off x shrinkage g, six-modality kernels, n=961
why: the parallel F-BERT session measured cross-modality CKA 0.68 on their chain but 0.34 for a pretrained deep model, and found on their own chain that the kernel filter alone explains the difference (0.849/0.681 no-filter -> 0.362/0.315 filtered). Independent replication on our atlas and features.
setting: Ooi Schaefer-400 features, our task extraction, alpha=0.10, w=0.05 full-kernel mix, filter tau=0.5 sd and keep=150 when on
replication: the same 2x2 shape, same sign in every cell. Filter removes +0.41 at g=0.85 and +0.26 at g=0.97; without the filter a higher g makes kernels MORE redundant, with the filter a higher g makes them LESS redundant. Their explanation -- that the apparent shared component is the flat noise tail sitting near the kernel diagonal, which every modality shares because every subject has the same diagonal -- predicts exactly this sign flip.
g1_note: g=1.00 degenerates numerically (trace of the alpha-weighted matrix goes to 0), so the sweep reports 0.85/0.92/0.95/0.97 only.
consequence: the cross-modality CKA number is not a property of the atlas or the preprocessing; it is a property of whether the filter is on. Any comparison of 'modality redundancy' across papers must state it.
